A: Maya's software company offered her the lead architect role, but it requires relocating to Toronto for eighteen months. Taking it would put her on track for an executive position, while leaving means missing Sunday dinners and the daily support she shares with her recently widowed sister. Should Maya accept the promotion or remain near her family?
B: After years painting sets for the same neighborhood theater, Luis has been invited to design a major touring production. The contract could establish his national reputation, yet rehearsals would keep him away through the final season with the close ensemble that trained him and depends on his presence. Should Luis join the tour or finish the season with his theater community?
C: A payment outage has trapped thousands of customers at checkout, and Priya is the only engineer who understands the failing service. She has a severe migraine and her doctor told her to rest in darkness, but the overnight support team cannot restore purchases without her guidance. Should Priya log in to lead the repair or protect her health and sleep?

A: Nora has been offered a solo exhibition at a prestigious Berlin gallery during the month her local printmaking collective is preparing its tenth anniversary show. Berlin could transform her career, but accepting would leave the five artists who built the collective with her to mount their milestone event alone. Should Nora pursue the solo exhibition or stay with her longtime collaborators?
B: A professional cycling team wants Darius to attend its distant development camp immediately, giving him his first credible route into elite racing. His neighborhood club, where his closest friends train together, is entering a regional relay that same month and has no replacement rider. Should Darius leave for the development camp or race beside his club?
C: Elena bought a demanding piano method course to prepare for an audition six months away. Tonight's scheduled practice covers scales she dislikes, while her favorite film has just appeared online and her friends are gathering to watch it with takeout. Skipping one evening would feel pleasant but weaken the routine she needs to improve. Should Elena practice or join the film night?

A: Jonah can enter an accelerated doctoral program that promises early publications and a strong academic career, but its schedule would end the weekly study circle he has shared with three close classmates since freshman year. Staying in the regular program preserves those friendships and their mutual support but slows his progress. Should Jonah accelerate alone or continue alongside his study group?
B: The owner of a renowned vineyard has offered Amara an apprenticeship that could lead to managing her own estate. It begins during harvest, when her family's small farm relies on everyone working and eating together, a tradition that has kept the household close for decades. Should Amara take the vineyard opportunity or spend another harvest with her family?
C: A school board wants new history workbooks distributed before Monday so classes can start the revised curriculum on time. Editor Caleb found conflicting dates and poorly sourced maps that require another week to verify; delaying leaves teachers without materials, while printing now may put lasting errors in every classroom. Should Caleb approve immediate printing or hold the workbooks for careful correction?

A: Ravi has qualified for a national young farmers competition whose winner receives enough investment to expand a greenhouse business. The final occurs during the cooperative's annual planting weekend, when his closest neighbors share equipment and count on his seed drill. Should Ravi travel to compete for expansion funding or plant beside the cooperative that has supported him?
B: Promotion to district fire captain would give Tessa greater responsibility and the career she has worked toward, but the post uses rotating stations across the county. She would lose daily shifts with the crew whose members helped raise her children and gather at her home every Friday. Should Tessa accept the captaincy or remain with her current station crew?
C: After twisting his knee, orchard manager Owen was told to avoid slopes for a week. A sudden frost is forecast tonight, and two inexperienced workers need him to guide the placement of heaters among the hillside trees; without him, much of the crop may be lost. Should Owen work the orchard despite the risk of worsening his injury or follow his recovery instructions?

A: Selene's bakery has been selected for a lucrative airport concession that could turn her single shop into a regional brand. Running it requires closing the original counter for six months, ending the morning routine she shares with loyal staff and neighbors who helped the bakery survive. Should Selene pursue the airport expansion or keep serving her established neighborhood circle?
B: Kenji's friends built a small open-source project together after work, and their weekly sessions became his main social anchor. A venture fund now wants him to develop it full-time in San Francisco without the others, offering the chance to create a major company. Should Kenji relocate to pursue the venture or keep building with his close-knit team?
C: For forty years, Ana's family restaurant has handwritten every order and displayed the paper tickets along the kitchen rail. A tablet system would reduce mistakes and simplify accounting, but her parents and regular customers see the visible tickets as part of the restaurant's character. Should Ana introduce digital ordering or preserve the family's familiar method?

A: Biologist Evan has saved a small emergency fund while working on short contracts. His former lab technician calls because her elderly cat needs surgery by Friday and she cannot cover the final eight hundred dollars; lending it may save the cat but leave Evan unable to pay rent if his contract ends. Should Evan provide the surgery money or preserve his emergency savings?
B: Adjunct lecturer Farah has enough set aside to replace her unreliable car before winter. A student she mentors has been accepted to a teaching conference but cannot afford the registration and train fare, and missing it could close an early career opportunity. Should Farah fund the student's trip or keep the money for dependable transportation?
C: During a joint experiment, Leah discovers that her longtime colleague Marcus entered several measurements incorrectly, making their celebrated result unsupported. Reporting the error before publication protects the scientific record but could cost Marcus his fellowship and damage a friendship built over twelve years. Should Leah disclose the faulty measurements to the journal or protect Marcus from the consequences?

A: Semi-professional goalkeeper Malik has saved his match fees for physiotherapy after recurring shoulder pain. His teammate's guide dog develops an infection requiring immediate treatment, and the teammate cannot cover the clinic deposit until payday. Paying would help the dog today but could leave Malik unable to treat his own injury. Should Malik cover the veterinary deposit or retain his therapy savings?
B: Library assistant Grace keeps three months of rent untouched because her hours may soon be cut. A coworker whose apartment flooded needs a hotel room for herself and her young son tonight, and local shelters are full. Should Grace pay for their temporary room or keep the money that protects her own housing if her income falls?
C: A rowing club asks captain Imani to tell the full team about her panic attacks after one struck during practice. Sharing the details could help teammates respond calmly and explain her occasional absences, but it would expose medical information she has kept private even from friends. Should Imani discuss her panic attacks with the team or keep that part of her life confidential?

A: Nurse Daniel keeps cash for a deposit on a safer apartment after repeated break-ins on his street. A discharged patient he has come to know needs a portable oxygen battery that insurance will not cover, and without it she cannot attend her daughter's wedding. Should Daniel buy the battery for her or protect his plan to move?
B: Mei reserved the month's remaining shop income to repair the freezer that protects her catering inventory. Her longtime delivery driver faces eviction with his daughter after an unexpected medical bill and asks for the exact amount Mei saved. Should Mei lend him the money and risk spoiled stock or secure the equipment her business depends on?
C: A rural hospital offers resident physician Sofia a competitive surgical fellowship that would speed her path toward becoming a specialist. Accepting means leaving the small ward team and patients she has served for three years, including colleagues who became her closest friends. Should Sofia take the fellowship or remain with the hospital community where she belongs?

A: Bus dispatcher Andre has saved enough to cover his mortgage during the agency's expected summer layoffs. A driver on his shift needs a specialized hearing aid to remain licensed, but her insurer denied the claim and she may lose her job next week. Should Andre help purchase the hearing aid or preserve his mortgage reserve?
B: Chemist Rosa planned to use her modest patent payment to clear a high-interest credit card. A graduate assistant in her lab needs dental surgery for a painful infection and has no family who can help, but covering it would keep Rosa in debt for another year. Should Rosa pay for the assistant's surgery or restore her own financial stability?
C: City planner Theo wants to replace two downtown parking lanes with protected bicycle lanes after studying the crash data. His parents, neighbors, and longtime friends all oppose the change and expect him to defend local parking at the public hearing. Should Theo present his preferred bicycle plan or endorse the position that would retain their approval?

A: Nadia has put aside the stipend from organizing a community garden to replace her broken laptop, which she needs for paid freelance work. A volunteer she knows is sleeping in his car and needs the same amount for a room deposit before cold weather arrives. Should Nadia fund his deposit or keep the money for her essential work equipment?
B: Ceramicist Joel keeps his market earnings as a cushion for months when few pieces sell. A fellow studio member's kiln accident injured her rabbit, and the emergency clinic requires payment tonight that she cannot raise. Should Joel use his cushion to cover the rabbit's treatment or retain the savings that steady his own uncertain income?
C: While coordinating a neighborhood playground rebuild, Aisha learns that she previously received treatment for a gambling addiction. Telling the volunteer committee could explain why she insists on dual signatures for every purchase and encourage frank financial oversight, but it would reveal a history she has shared with almost nobody. Should Aisha disclose her past to the committee or keep it private?

A: Devon promised to supervise a critical database migration because the junior engineers have never performed one. On the scheduled night, he develops a high fever and dizziness; postponement would interrupt a client's launch, but staying online until dawn may deepen his illness. Should Devon lead the migration as promised or stop working to recover?
B: Midwife Hana has completed a double shift when a patient she supported throughout pregnancy goes into complicated labor. The replacement midwife is qualified but unfamiliar with the patient's history, while Hana is shaking from fatigue and needs sleep to recover safely. Should Hana remain for the birth she promised to attend or hand over care and rest?
C: Developer Arjun can spend a month experimenting with an unfamiliar database that might make his new app remarkably flexible, though its limitations are still unclear. The proven system offers predictable performance and reliable backups but restricts several features he hopes to discover. Should Arjun explore the uncertain technology or build with the safer established platform?

A: Stage manager Ruth promised to call every cue for her community theater's opening night, and no understudy knows the complicated lighting sequence. Hours before curtain she experiences chest pain and is advised to seek immediate evaluation; canceling disappoints a sold-out audience, while continuing could endanger her health. Should Ruth go to the hospital or fulfill her opening-night responsibility?
B: Cafe owner Ben has bronchitis and his doctor prescribed two days of complete rest. His only employee calls out just before a prepaid memorial reception, leaving the grieving family without the meal Ben agreed to provide. Should Ben open the kitchen and honor the booking or close the cafe to protect his recovery?
C: A gallery charges every exhibitor the same late fee when work arrives after the installation deadline. Curator Mina's former teacher misses it because she has been caring for her terminally ill husband and cannot afford the charge, though others have paid after difficult weeks. Should Mina waive the fee for her teacher or enforce the rule equally?
